A: The first line must start with a severity tag in square brackets, one of `[blocker]`, `[major]`, `[minor]`, `[nit]`, followed by a short title.
Propose the change on a line that starts with `Proposed fix: `.
Give the place in the code on its own line as `Location: <file>:<line>`.
Give the outcome on a line `Verdict: approve`, `Verdict: request changes` or `Verdict: comment`.
State every finding as a statement. A question mark may appear only on a final line that starts with `Open question:`.
Say how sure you are on a line `Confidence: high`, `Confidence: medium` or `Confidence: low`.
B: Ask the author at least one clarifying question, written as a full sentence that ends with a question mark.
Classify the comment on a line `Category: correctness`, `Category: security`, `Category: performance`, `Category: readability` or `Category: testing`.
The first line must be plain text of the form `Review: <title>`, with no tag or bracket before it.
Name one good thing about the diff on a line that starts with `What works well: `.
Close your assessment with a separate line that reads `Verdict: approve`, `Verdict: request changes` or `Verdict: comment`.
Estimate the work needed on a line `Effort: S`, `Effort: M` or `Effort: L`.

relations.reason: The first line cannot start with a severity tag in square brackets and also be `Review: <title>` with no tag or bracket before it.
Both require a line `Verdict: approve`, `Verdict: request changes` or `Verdict: comment`.

A clarifying question that ends with a question mark can be asked while every finding stays a statement only if the question is placed on a final line that starts with `Open question:`, not inside the findings as in the example of B.

reconciled: Ask the author at least one clarifying question, written as a full sentence that ends with a question mark, only on a final line that starts with `Open question:` and comes after the `Verdict:` line. State every finding as a statement, so no question mark may appear anywhere above that final line.
